newsitem.title: USA: Experts ready to move ship from Florida reef.
newsitem.headline: Experts ready to move ship from Florida reef.

text.p: Salvage experts were nearly ready to drag the container ship Houston from the sand and coral of the National Marine Sanctuary where it has been stuck since Sunday, a Coast Guard spokesman said on Saturday.
Salvage experts hope to lighten the Houston's load enough so tug boats can pull the ship free during the Saturday evening high tide at 8:52 p.m. EST (0152 GMT on Sunday).
An empty fuel barge arrived at the Houston early on Saturday, and salvage experts were transferring 540,000 gallons (2.044 million litres) of engine fuel from the stranded ship.
"They're well into the pumping and it should be completed within the next several hours," Coast Guard spokesman Marcus Woodring said.

The Houston, owned by the Mexican freight company Transportacion Maritima Mexican, plowed into a section of reef in the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary late on Sunday. The ship violated a special no-shipping zone designed to protect the fragile coral reef area, which was covered by the rising sea millions of years ago.
Its crew waited nearly six hours before notifying the U.S. Coast Guard the ship was stranded.

While the fuel was being transferred into the barge, salvage experts were pumping sea water into the Houston's ballast area to compensate, Woodring said. The sea water would only be pumped out when technicians were ready to move the ship, to minimize further damage to the reef.

Environmentalists consider the mishap a close call for the nearby Western Sambos Ecological Reserve, which is the heart of the lower Keys reef ecosystem. None of the freighter's fuel had leaked by Saturday, the Coast Guard said.
